## What you did
- Traced Orbitly's ~8% iOS funnel drop to your own SDK: kestrel-ios 3.2.0 switched `event_id` to a per-session counter, so #240's event_id-only dedupe silently dropped ~1.18M legitimate Orbitly events (~8.1% of their iOS volume); Zest's pilot app lost 3,812 the same way [1].
- Fixed it in PR #247, re-keying the dedupe on (project, device, event_id) so replays stay dropped and distinct events survive, with maya as reviewer [1][2].
- Drafted the note asking the iOS team to restore UUIDs in 3.2.1 before this bites again [1].

## What changed
- maya confirms the logic is right, will approve once CI is green, and wants your Orbitly drop count for Thursday's call with Orbitly [2].
- Postmortem #233 is final; Noa presents it at Friday's incident review (20/11) [3].

## What is still open
- #247 still needs green CI and maya's approval before merge [2].
- Send maya the figure (~1.18M events) for Thursday's Orbitly call [2].
- Only once #247 is deployed, replay from landing for `prj_0rb1` (and `prj_z3st`) from 13/11, then confirm `ingest_dedupe_dropped_total` stays near zero [1].
- Add the alert for the ingest dead-letter queue above 1,000 messages before Friday's review — it's on you from the prep session [7].
